A common cause is that the partial is rendered or swapped without the token: the base template's token only helps if the form is inside it or htmx sends it as a header. Two fixes: put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form in the partial, or set `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on the body so every hx-post carries it. Also check the view renders the partial with request context.
Action: look at the partial and the view to see which of these applies.

Use `useLayoutEffect` when you must measure or change the DOM before the browser paints, so the user never sees an in-between frame. Examples: placing a tooltip from getBoundingClientRect, or restoring scroll position after content changes. Everything else, like data fetching, subscriptions and logging, belongs in `useEffect`, which runs after paint.

They are different. Keep-alive in HTTP/1.1 only reuses a connection for one request at a time, so concurrent requests still need several connections or queue up. HTTP/2 multiplexing sends many requests in parallel as interleaved streams over a single connection, avoiding application-level head-of-line blocking (TCP-level blocking remains).
Action: none needed.

```ts
export function slugify(s: string, max = 64) { return s.normalize('NFKD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '').toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '').slice(0, max).replace(/-+$/, ''); }
```

There is a real difference. `structuredClone` keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, undefined and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, empties Maps and Sets, drops undefined, and throws on cycles. Neither copies functions, and class instances lose their prototype.
Action: none needed; I can reply on the PR with this if you want.
